audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side read "Skill" while content win[0..6] read Katarina/Katarina/Katarina/Katarina/Akali/Katarina/Akali. Two different answers to who wins each stage, and phases[4].why and phases[6].why both describe Katarina winning stages the content layer awards to Akali.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer exactly (Akali at Level 6 and 2+ items, Katarina elsewhere), and the prose in whys[4]/whys[6], spikes[1] and spikes[3] all argue the same: Perfect Execution's two dashes dodge Death Lotus, and R2's execute plus Twilight Shroud beat kill-dependent resets late.
audit.corrected: phases[N].side aligned to the content layer and the packet; phases[4].why and phases[6].why rewritten so the sentence agrees with the new verdict.

audit.why: Spike placement is right and grounded: Katarina owns 3-5 (Q 11/10/9/8/7s and E 12/11/10/9/8s are free while Five Point Strike costs 110-70 energy), Akali's 6 is the flip (Perfect Execution 120/90/60s, two casts, execute), first item favours Katarina, 2+ items favours Akali.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it; Twilight Shroud's real duration-of-untargetability window was described without its 20/19/18/17/16s cooldown or Shuriken Flip's 16s rank-1 cooldown. Akali's Assassin's Mark auto-reset tell was absent everywhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot's text: Twilight Shroud makes her 'unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks', so a Shunpo cast at her inside it has no target and both charges are wasted. Assassin's Mark rings her target and empowers her next attack on exit — an auto-attack reset that is the actual opener tell, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field now carries Shroud 20s rank 1 and Shuriken Flip 16s rank 1; dosFull[0].d states the Assassin's Mark wind-up tell; tradeBad states the untargetability.

audit.why: 51.52% over 5091 games — the EVEN label and 5.5/10 rating already match.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] wrote "Five Point Strikes" — the ability is Five Point Strike.
